definitions.explanation: A loud call or shout used to encourage, coordinate action, or boost morale. Common in group activities, sports, and traditional arts.

examples.japanese: 「よいしょ！」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{士気|しき}→士気：19824_shiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上|あ}がった→上がる：00615_agaru⟧。
examples.english: The team's rallying cry raised morale.

examples.japanese: {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{終|お}わらず、⟦{実行|じっこう}→実行：03274_jikkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{移|うつ}す→移す：10122_utsusu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: It's important not to stop at just words but to put them into action.

notes:
WRITING:
{掛|か}け (to call out) + {声|ごえ} (voice). Literally "calling voice."

USAGE:
Used in many contexts: sports cheers, group labor ("heave-ho!"), martial arts shouts ({気合|きあい}い), and kabuki audience calls. The phrase {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧ means "to shout/call out."

The idiomatic expression {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧ or {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}{倒|だお}れ means "all talk and no action" — making bold declarations without following through.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧: to shout, to call out
- {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧: to move in time with the call
- {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}{倒|だお}れ: all talk, no action
- {掛|か}け{声|ごえ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{始|はじ}める: to start with a shout
